answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent influence to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to raw identity count. Like a vine that only grows where it has actually taken root, an agent earns weight gradually through completed tasks, peer attestations, and a small refundable stake that is slashed for fraud. A newcomer can send one pulse of activity, but cannot instantly command a plume of voting power: creating thousands of fake accounts multiplies no history and no stake, so the cost of forging a credible record exceeds any reward from a single vote.
